bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Energy cost and grid availability in manufacturing — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a risk: electricity constitutes a significant operating expense in the manufacture of water pumps, and escalating power tariffs, interruptions in grid availability and reliance on conventional energy sources may lead to higher production costs and disrupt manufacturing schedules. Mitigation is through energy-consumption tracking, energy-efficient technologies, renewable energy integration and peak demand management.
- Raw material and component sourcing concentration — BRSR flags that pumps require certain metals and components that may have limited global suppliers and be subject to price volatility or geopolitical risk; disruptions can delay production and impact margins. Mitigated by supplier diversification, long-term supply agreements, alternative materials and strategic inventory reserves.
- Workforce health and safety in heavy manufacturing — Employees are exposed to occupational risks from heavy equipment, electrical systems and movement of large or cumbersome materials; shortcomings in safety practices may lead to injuries, production disruption, regulatory consequences and reputational damage. Managed through stringent SOPs, periodic training, mandatory PPE, preventive maintenance and hazard/incident reporting.
- Talent attrition in a competitive renewable energy labour market — Permanent-employee turnover rose to 26.03% in FY2025-26 from 10.24% in FY2024-25. The Company attributes this to early attrition among freshers who were unwilling to work in the assigned domain despite it being communicated at campus hiring, and to newly established regional renewable-segment companies offering higher compensation and benefits.
- Single-activity / single-product concentration — The BRSR reports 100% of turnover from a single main activity - manufacture of electrical equipment and general/special purpose machinery - and 100% of turnover from the manufacture of pumps, leaving the business without a diversifying revenue line outside the pumping and allied equipment franchise.
- Dependence on government schemes and institutional buyers — Government institutions are described as a significant customer group, with the Company playing a vital role in flagship rural solarisation initiatives such as PM-KUSUM. Scheme design, tendering pace and policy change therefore drive a material share of demand.
- Export and geographic exposure — Export sales represented approximately 13.75% of total turnover during the reporting period, spread across more than 100 countries and served through international agencies, project developers and institutional buyers, exposing the business to overseas demand, currency and geopolitical conditions.
- External macro, policy, technology and climate factors flagged in the forward-looking statement — Management explicitly cautions that actual results may differ materially due to changes in economic conditions, government policies, regulatory developments, industry dynamics, technological advancements, competitive intensity, geopolitical events and climate-related risks.

- Continue investing in technology, backward integration, manufacturing expansion and operational excellence to strengthen the competitive edge
- Reduce environmental footprint, improve resource efficiency, conserve water and adopt circular manufacturing practices in support of India's Net Zero aspirations
- The Company follows a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy published in the Policies and Programmes section of its website, and the AGM notice puts a final dividend of `1 per equity share (10% of the `10 face value) for FY2025-26 to members for declaration. The Board reserves to itself the corporate strategy, major plans of action, risk policy, annual budgets and business plans, and the oversight of major capital expenditures, acquisitions and divestments, with the stated fiduciary aim of maximising shareholder value. - Circularity: embedding remanufacturing considerations into pump design to lower the need for virgin raw materials, improve resource and manufacturing efficiency and create revenue from refurbished and reconditioned products

Wholly owned subsidiary Shakti Energy Solutions Ltd., located in Pithampur (MP), currently does only captive production and has plans to sell to other players as well. demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Solar energy is positioned at the core of the business; management links growth to India's clean energy ambitions and agricultural progress
- An estimated 25% market share under the PM-KUSUM scheme, an integrated manufacturing ecosystem and a presence across 100+ countries are cited as the basis of a resilient business model capable of delivering scale
- Grid-connected solar pumping is expected to improve rural prosperity, reduce subsidy dependence and strengthen DISCOMs, which management frames as the demand opportunity in Indian agriculture
- Technology shift towards smart pumping systems, digital monitoring, IoT-enabled water management and energy optimisation is described as defining future demand
- Investments in R&D and intellectual property (15 patents, a DSIR-recognised R&D centre) and in next-generation solar technologies are cited as the drivers of future positioning
- Management explicitly cautions that outcomes may differ due to economic conditions, government policies, regulatory developments, industry dynamics, technological advancements, competitive intensity, geopolitical events and climate-related risks

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 margins hit by 6-7% raw material inflation (copper, steel, silicon), 3-4% lower realization from Magel Tyala scheme, and 2-3% operating leverage benefit; Export margins ~10% higher than domestic.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority on working capital normalization (receivables reduced by INR 420cr in Q4); Funding growth via internal accruals to avoid undue leverage.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Shakti Pumps has committed `17,000 Mn to a capacity expansion programme, described in the FY26 Key Milestones as covering an advanced 2.2 GW solar manufacturing platform, a doubling of capacity for pumps, motors, VFDs and solar structures, and the establishment of a manufacturing facility for EV motors, controllers and chargers under Shakti EV Mobility Pvt. Ltd. The Corporate Overview frames this as phased capacity build-out - 'continuous investments in R&D, integrated manufacturing, automation and phased capacity including 2.2 GW Solar DCR Cell and PV Module manufacturing' - positioned as a long-term competitive advantage through backward integration. The existing footprint is four integrated manufacturing facilities headquartered at Pithampur, Madhya Pradesh, with backward-integrated capability across pumps, motors, controllers, inverters, VFDs, solar structures and allied components; earlier milestones record establishment of an SEZ unit and expansion of the core facility to 5,00,000 pump capacity. Wholly owned subsidiary Shakti Energy Solutions Ltd., located in Pithampur (MP), currently does only captive production and has plans to sell to other players as well. The routed sections give no commissioning, ramp-up or completion dates for the announced expansion, and no project-wise capex split.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated manufacturing ecosystem: backward-integrated capabilities across pumps, motors, controllers, inverters, VFDs, solar structures and allied components enabling superior quality control, faster execution and operational efficiency
- Leadership in solar pumping with an estimated ~25% market share under PM-KUSUM and an installed base of 2.36+ lakh solar pumps to date
- Diversified clean-energy portfolio spanning solar pumping, rooftop solar, smart pumping technologies and EV motors/controllers/chargers
- Global market reach across 100+ countries with a diversified customer base of government projects, industrial customers, OEMs, retail and exports
- Intellectual property and R&D depth: 15 patents including a US patent for energy-efficient motor technology, and a DSIR-recognised R&D centre
- Distribution and service footprint in India built on a network of over 500 dealers
- Over four decades of manufacturing experience in pumping solutions

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Delay in KUSUM 2.0 announcement; Sustained high raw material prices; Payment delays from state discoms despite recent improvements; Competitive intensity in L1 tenders.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
